The DP2020A5022 is a definite purpose contactor from Resideo (Honeywell Home), rated 20 amps and built with 1 pole and a 24 Vac coil. It is the switch that lets a low-power control circuit start a compressor, a condenser fan, or an electric heat bank.

A definite purpose contactor is sized for one job rather than for general industrial duty, which is why it costs a fraction of a general purpose starter and still carries the inrush of an air conditioning compressor. The coil pulls the contacts closed when the thermostat or control board calls; when the call drops, spring pressure opens them.

A single-pole contactor switches one leg of the supply and leaves the other connected. It is the common arrangement on residential condensing units, where the manufacturer has already accounted for the unswitched leg in the unit wiring.

The 24 Vac coil is driven straight from the low-voltage control transformer, so the thermostat circuit never carries line current.

Replacement humidifier pad from Resideo (Honeywell Home), part number HC26P1002/U.

The pad is the part of an evaporative humidifier that actually does the work. Water runs across it, house air passes through it, and the water leaves as vapor. Mineral scale builds on the pad as that happens, and a scaled pad passes air without evaporating much of anything.

Replace the pad at the start of each heating season. A humidifier that will not hold setpoint has usually not failed — it is running on a pad that has turned to rock.

Scale build-up is faster on hard water, and a pad that would last a season on soft water can be finished by February on a well. If the unit sounds like it is running but the humidity reading will not climb, pull the pad and look at it before troubleshooting anything electrical.

Fitting the correct pad matters more than it looks. The pad has to fill its frame for the air to pass through it rather than around it, and an undersized or wrong-profile pad lets the airstream bypass the water entirely.

The R8239A1052 is a fan center from Resideo (Honeywell Home): a control transformer and a relay in one enclosure, rated 40 VA, with SPDT contacts.

A fan center is what lets a low-voltage thermostat run a line-voltage blower. The transformer makes the 24 V control power, the relay carries the blower current, and both live in a box that mounts on the furnace or air handler instead of being assembled from loose parts.

SPDT contacts give a normally open and a normally closed set from the same relay, so the same fan center can run a blower on a call and drop a damper or an interlock at the same time.

Note on category: this part is listed under aquastats, but it is a fan center, not a boiler water temperature control. It does not sense temperature.

The DR90A3000 is a whole-home dehumidification system from Resideo (Honeywell Home). It is ducted into the home rather than set in a room, so one unit pulls moisture out of the whole house instead of one basement corner.

Whole-home dehumidification solves the problem an air conditioner cannot: on a mild humid day the cooling load is too small to run the compressor long enough to wring out the air, and the house ends up cool and clammy. A ducted dehumidifier runs on humidity alone, independent of the call for cooling.

Because it works on the whole duct system, it also holds humidity down in the rooms furthest from the air handler — the ones that are always the worst in a house with a portable unit in the basement.

  • Brand: Resideo (Honeywell Home)
  • Manufacturer Part #: DR90A3000/U
  • Type: Whole-home ducted dehumidifier
  • Category: Dehumidifiers

Advanced Electrode Humidifier Replacement Cylinder — genuine Resideo (Honeywell Home) service part, number HM750ACYL/U.

Whole-home humidifiers and dehumidifiers run through an entire heating or cooling season without being looked at, and the parts that fail are the ones that see water and cycling: solenoids, boards, cylinders and filters. Replacing the failed part is what keeps an unit that is otherwise sound out of the landfill.

Check the model number on the unit label before ordering. Resideo humidifier platforms share a family name but not always a part, and a board or solenoid from the neighbouring model will not drop in.

Two failures account for most humidifier service calls. A solenoid that will not open leaves the pad dry and the house at whatever humidity the weather gives it; a solenoid that will not close runs water through the unit and down the drain all season, which shows up on the water bill long before anyone notices the humidity is high.

Hard water shortens the life of every wetted part in a humidifier. Where the supply is hard, an in-line scale filter and a fresh pad each season do more for the unit than any other maintenance.

  • Manufacturer Part #: HM750ACYL/U
  • Category: Humidifier Parts

This is a manual reset high limit. Once it trips, the control stays open until someone presses the button — the boiler does not simply restart when the water cools. That is deliberate: a high limit trip means something went wrong upstream, and a self-resetting limit would hide it.

The 66 in capillary lets the sensing bulb sit in the boiler while the control body mounts where it can be reached and wired.

As a high limit, this control has one job that matters more than the rest: it stops the burner before the boiler gets away. Everything else in the heating system is comfort; the high limit is safety.

When you replace an aquastat, match the temperature range, the switch action and the differential to the control coming out, not to the boiler nameplate. A boiler will happily run on a control with the wrong range — it will simply cycle badly, or trip a limit that was never meant to be the working control.

The sensing bulb belongs in an immersion well, filled with heat conductive compound, threaded into the tapping the boiler manufacturer provided for it. A bulb strapped to the outside of a pipe reads the pipe, not the water, and it reads it late.

Replacement humidifier pad from Resideo (Honeywell Home), part number HC26E1004/U, for the HE265 and HE365 humidifiers.

The pad is the part of an evaporative humidifier that actually does the work. Water runs across it, house air passes through it, and the water leaves as vapor. Mineral scale builds on the pad as that happens, and a scaled pad passes air without evaporating much of anything.

Replace the pad at the start of each heating season. A humidifier that will not hold setpoint has usually not failed — it is running on a pad that has turned to rock.

Scale build-up is faster on hard water, and a pad that would last a season on soft water can be finished by February on a well. If the unit sounds like it is running but the humidity reading will not climb, pull the pad and look at it before troubleshooting anything electrical.

Fitting the correct pad matters more than it looks. The pad has to fill its frame for the air to pass through it rather than around it, and an undersized or wrong-profile pad lets the airstream bypass the water entirely.

This pad carries an AgION antimicrobial coating, which limits the growth that otherwise takes hold on a surface that stays damp all winter.

The L7224U1002 is an universal electronic oil aquastat from Resideo (Honeywell Home). It replaces the mechanical high-limit and circulator controls on an oil-fired boiler with a single electronic control, and it speaks EnviraCOM, so the boiler can report to a compatible thermostat or service tool.

The advantage of an electronic aquastat over a bimetal control is that it can run a thermal targeting strategy: instead of holding the boiler at one high limit all winter, it lowers the target when the heating load is light and raises it when the house is actually calling hard. On an oil boiler that spends most of the season under part load, that is where the fuel saving comes from.

Universal means one control covers a range of applications that used to need different part numbers, which is worth as much to a service truck as it is to the installation.
